concept.name: Portfolio
concept.definition: The combined holdings of stocks, bonds, commodities, real estate, and other investments owned by an individual or institutional investor, analyzed and managed as a single unit.
concept.intuition: Your portfolio is the whole basket of things you own, not any single holding; its behavior is what you actually experience as an investor.
concept.mechanics: A portfolio is characterized by a weight vector w (each w_i is the fraction of value in asset i, weights summing to 1). Its return is the weighted sum of asset returns, while its risk depends on the full covariance structure of the components, not just their individual volatilities.
concept.formula: R_p = sum_i w_i * R_i, with sum_i w_i = 1, where w_i is the value weight of asset i and R_i its return.
concept.failure_modes: Treating a collection of separate accounts or funds as independent obscures aggregate exposures: overlapping holdings and shared factor bets can make a 'many-fund' portfolio far more concentrated than it looks.
concept.misconceptions: Owning many different funds does not automatically make a portfolio diversified; what matters is how the underlying returns co-move, not the count of positions.
concept.example: An investor holding 60% in a total stock market index fund, 30% in a bond index fund, and 10% in a money market fund has one portfolio whose return each month is 0.6*R_stocks + 0.3*R_bonds + 0.1*R_cash.
